subject: Admin activity logging: scope, retention buckets, and emergency export SLA
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@greenlinehealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on admin logs & export options

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. Greenline is finalizing the SIG and SOC 2 evidence bundle and our audit team wants a concise description of what "admin activity" includes for Redwood, how long each category is retained, and what export formats/SLAs you offer for an on-demand evidence pull. Specifically they asked: 

- Which admin events are captured (examples: role changes, account provisioning, API key ops, auth failures, console logins, model promotion)?
- Retention windows by event class and whether differential/incremental snapshots are possible.
- Export format options (JSONL, Parquet, signed manifest) and whether extracts include checksums and HMACs for chain-of-custody.
- Typical turnaround time for an ad-hoc evidence request and any emergency (legal/subpoena) SLA.

If you can send a short summary and any sample manifest we can include in the evidence bundle.

Appreciate it — Alice
Compliance, Greenline Health

P.S. we may need a small sample (2-3 days) with PII redacted for the SOC 2 audit team.
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on admin logs & export options

Alice — thanks for the clear list. High level answer below; I attached a compact "admin logging matrix" CSV and a sample manifest for a 72-hour export. If you need a tailored sample (PII-scrubbed) we can arrange that — we'll need a signed NDA addendum for the sample with PII.

What we capture (examples):
- Identity & access events: console logins (OKTA/OIDC assertions), MFA failures/successes, OAuth token grants, SSO provider metadata.
- Admin lifecycle: user creation/deactivation, role & group membership changes, privilege escalations, service account creation/rotation.
- Configuration changes: model promotion/deployment events, inference-config changes, autoscaling policy edits, routing rule updates.
- API & control-plane ops: API key creation/revoke, admin API calls (who/what/when/params), provisioning actions.
- Policy & consent events: consent revocations, data-retention flag changes.
- Operator actions: access to customer-specific private deployments (VPC on-prem handoffs, console remote sessions).

Retention buckets (default):
- 30 days: high-volume operational traces (short-term debug logs, ephemeral session traces).
- 1 year: most admin events (role changes, API key ops, major config edits).
- 3 years: security-sensitive events (privilege escalations, audit manifests, evidence snapshots) — available under enterprise contracts.
- 7 years: legal/retention hold for customers with explicit contractual requirements (special add-on).

Notes: retention is configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted defaults above. We keep immutable daily snapshots for the first 90 days and incremental deltas thereafter to support efficient on-demand bundles.

Export formats & integrity: 
- Supported export formats: JSONL (per-event), Parquet (columnar), and compressed tarballs of JSONL + manifest.
- Each export includes: signed manifest.json (SHA256 checksums per file), export metadata (time window, region, retention-tags), and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the manifest (customer KMS or Redwood attestation key).
- Delivery modes: S3 presigned URL (time-limited), secure SFTP push, or encrypted handoff to customer-managed bucket.

Access & redaction:
- We can produce PII-scrubbed samples using deterministic redaction plus tokenization for identifiers. Redaction rules are documented and can be adjusted per mutual agreement.
- Sampling: full-window extracts are standard; if the dataset is large we can provide statistically representative samples as requested.

SLAs:
- Standard on-demand evidence request (non-legal): 48–72 business hours for up to 7 days of data; longer windows negotiated.
- Priority compliance SLA (SOC 2 audit window): 24–48 hours (requires SOC-scope ticket + verification).
- Emergency/legal/ subpoena: we offer an escalation path — emergency export SLA is 4 hours for customers on Platinum/Enterprise support (with pre-authorized contacts and legal checklist). For hosted customers without an enterprise SLA we'll engage legal and aim for 24 hours.

Chain-of-custody & attestations:
- We keep an auditable manifest history and signatures; manifests are timestamped and stored in an immutable store with retention that matches the evidence snapshot retention policy.
- We can provide an attestation letter describing extraction steps, hash verification instructions, and a contact for notarization requests.

Next steps / action items:
1) I'll drop a redacted 3-day sample (JSONL) into the Drive link once we have the addendum signed.
2) Marissa — can you confirm the HMAC signing key procedure and point to the sample manifest so I can share it externally?
3) Karthik / Logan — please confirm the emergency export runbook and estimated time to spin a 7-day full export for Greenline (hosted account GH-9913).

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood-admin-logging-matrix-20250422.csv, s3-export-sample-manifest.json
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity logging: scope, retention buckets, and emergency export SLA

Looping in operational runbook details. Quick clarifications: 

- HMAC/signing: manifests are signed with Redwood's attestation key by default; for customers who supply a KMS key we sign the manifest with a per-export key-wrapping process and include key metadata in the manifest.
- Export size & pragmatic approach: for >30 days we build a delta-series (daily Parquet slices) and provide a small index file so the auditor can validate continuity without downloading the full dataset.
- For PII-scrubbed samples we apply reversible tokenization (audit-only) when requested by legal; irreversible redaction only when customer requests.

Naomi — I can generate a 72-hour Parquet sample and the signed manifest tonight. Logan and I will prepare the emergency-runbook snippet for the 4-hour SLA (what automation we require, who is the on-call approver).

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, Alice Martin <alice.martin@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Admin activity logging: scope, retention buckets, and emergency export SLA

Alice / Naomi — final operational notes for Greenline: 

- For GH-9913 (hosted): a standard 7-day full admin export (JSONL, compressed) is ~4.2GB; Parquet compression reduces that to ~1.1GB. Expect a 24–36 hour job for full rebuild + manifest on our standard infra.
- Emergency 4-hour SLA requires pre-approved emergency contacts (legal + security) and a signed expedited request form; we'll use an elevated job priority queue and s3 presigned delivery.
- Chain of custody verification steps we will provide to the auditor: 1) verify manifest signature against attestation key; 2) validate each file checksum; 3) cross-check event counts in manifest index.

Karthik — when you have a quick note on how we route extracts for Dedicated vs Hosted (encryption-in-transit to customer-managed buckets), drop it here and I'll add to the Drive doc.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Infra Operations, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
